rules.statement: In a pre-release project, don't add a compatibility shim, migration note or wording that contrasts the product with an earlier state; describe the product only as it is now.
rules.why: ADR-0015: a pre-release product has no released users to migrate, so texts and code describe only the current state.
rules.check: In a pre-release project's diff, look for obsolete-forwarding members or aliases kept for old callers, 'previously'/'now'/'no longer' wording in docs or changelog, and migration sections.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, don't mark changes as breaking: no `**Breaking:**` changelog label, no conventional-commit `!` marker and no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in commit messages or pull request titles.
rules.why: ADR-0015: before the first release nothing can break for users, so breaking-change markers misdescribe the product.
rules.check: Look in CHANGELOG.md, commit messages and the PR title for `**Breaking:**`, `feat!:`-style markers or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project, keep the changelog's `## [Unreleased]` section a catalog under only `### Added` and `### Security` headings.
rules.why: ADR-0015: with no prior release, every entry is something the product has, so Changed/Removed/Fixed/Deprecated sections don't apply.
rules.check: Check CHANGELOG.md's `## [Unreleased]` section for any subsection other than `### Added` and `### Security`.

rules.statement: Don't skip or weaken tests, swallow errors, hard-code values or leave TODOs to make a change pass its checks.
rules.why: These shortcuts make checks pass while the required behavior isn't actually delivered.
rules.check: Look for new Skip attributes, loosened assertions or deleted test cases, empty or broad catch blocks, magic literals standing in for computed or configured values, and new TODO/FIXME comments.
